messages.subject: Instruction - Maybrook v Helmsworth (HC-450 plant engineering)
messages.plaintextBody:
Dear Mr Penrith,

Thank you for agreeing to act. I attach our formal letter of instruction. In summary we need your opinion on the cause of the four failures (inherent defect vs misuse), whether the plant could sustain 320 t/h, and on Helmsworth's response times. The plant and the replaced components are available for inspection at the Aldforth site; Paul Hedges will arrange access.

Your duty is to the Court under CPR Part 35.

Kind regards,
Tom

Tom Gallagher | Associate
Whitfield Carter LLP | 22 Bishopsgate, London EC2N 4BQ
T +44 (0)20 7946 0500
Confidential and may be legally privileged.

messages.subject: RE: Instruction - Maybrook v Helmsworth (HC-450 plant engineering)
messages.plaintextBody:
Tom,

Received, thank you. I'll arrange to inspect next week. From the photographs the bearing failures look like fatigue/overload rather than impact, which would point away from the tramp-metal theory, but I'll confirm after examining the components and the weighbridge data.

David Penrith
Penrith Crushing & Screening Consultants Ltd
